entry_item.definition: T. rdo rje; S. vajra. Thunderbolt; diamond; the all-destroying, indestructible weapon of Xormusda (Indra) was early used metaphorically to suggest immutability, permanency, and the like. In late Buddhism it became the symbol of the absolute. See kølgen and bej-e. In the mystical sphere it assumed connotations of the linga (phallus) in Hinduism, its counterpart (the yoni) being the xongxu. As a ritualist implement it may have developed out of the serege. The vacir, made of metal, 4-5 inches long, resembles an open-worked dumbell . It and the xongxu symbolize the male deity and its female counterpart (T. nus pa, S. cakti).

example.definition: T. Rdo rje gdan; S. Vajrasana. Thunderbolt seat, name of the seat on which Sagjamuni, while meditating, found enlightenment.
